sn47.5:1.2: There the Blessed One said this:
sn47.5:1.3: “Bhikkhus, if one were to say of anything ‘a heap of the unwholesome,’ it is about the five hindrances that one could rightly say this.
sn47.5:1.4: For this is a complete heap of the unwholesome, that is, the five hindrances.
sn47.5:1.6: The hindrance of sensual desire, the hindrance of ill will, the hindrance of sloth and torpor, the hindrance of restlessness and remorse, the hindrance of doubt.
sn47.5:1.7: If one were to say of anything ‘a heap of the unwholesome,’ it is about these five hindrances that one could rightly say this.
sn47.5:1.8: For this is a complete heap of the unwholesome, that is, the five hindrances.
sn47.5:2.1: “If, bhikkhus, one were to say of anything ‘a heap of the wholesome, ’ it is about the four establishments of mindfulness that one could rightly say this.
sn47.5:2.2: For this is a complete heap of the wholesome, that is, the four establishments of mindfulness.
sn47.5:2.4: Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.
sn47.5:2.5: He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings …
sn47.5:2.7: phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.
sn47.5:2.8: If one were to say of anything ‘a heap of the wholesome, ’ it is about these four establishments of mindfulness that one could rightly say this.
sn47.5:2.9: For this is a complete heap of the wholesome, that is, the four establishments of mindfulness.”
